correctness.rationale: The exact witness-count factorization follows from the surjective diagonal-block quotient of the finite abelian p-group endomorphism ring and its constant-size fibers. Matrix-avoidance at dimension m>=2 is proved by counting fixed-vector pairs, giving a strict upper bound less than |GL_m|/(p-1) for each bad translate. Singleton diagonal blocks are independent uniform scalars for independent uniform automorphisms; failure at k=p-1 occurs precisely when all p-1 nonzero residues appear. Multiplying independent occupancy probabilities proves the formula. Exact finite computations confirmed representative boundary cases, including all 11,664 automorphism pairs of C3+C9; finite tests are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary preprint proves the homocyclic existence lemma and supplies the block decomposition, and these are explicitly not claimed as new. Its stated results and application sections do not determine a universal random-tuple endpoint probability or exact witness-count fiber formula. The complete published automorphism-count proof determines a single fixed-point-free condition; it does not give the multiple-input endpoint distribution. Its characteristic-two universal criterion, due to Gross, already covers that part of the stated boundary and is credited as prior. Full-text primary inspection and semantic searches of published results plus accessible prior claims identified no equivalent exact probability. Historical priority and obscure matrix-covering analogues remain risks.

value.rationale: The exact distribution is a complete natural endpoint invariant for every finite abelian p-group. It reveals that all complicated exponent and higher-rank data cancel: only the number of singleton elementary-divisor multiplicities survives in the probability. This sharp universal-versus-obstructed threshold, full factorization of witness counts, mixed-exponent examples and asymptotic transition add structural information to an explicit recently opened boundary question, without claiming its nonlinear form solved.
